slides.claim_category: authored explanation or proposed learning activity

claim_checks.claim: Self-assessment means judging your own work and learning against explicit criteria, then using that judgment to improve.
claim_checks.boundary: This is a defensible formative definition, rather than an exhaustive account of all summative and informal uses of self-assessment. No AI-feedback validation is implied.

claim_checks.evidence: Andrade’s review supports the criterion-referenced formative framing. It does not validate the workshop or an AI feedback system, and the slide makes no such claim.

slides.title: AI tutoring can improve learning
slides.claim_category: published research claim with population and outcome limits

claim_checks.claim: 194 eligible students at Harvard · Two physics lessons · Immediate post-tests with a purpose-built tutor. The AI-tutor condition produced higher immediate test scores than an active-learning class, with less time on task.
claim_checks.boundary: One course and immediate post-tests; time measures differ by condition. Does not establish durable learning or general commercial-chatbot effects.

claim_checks.claim: 194 eligible Harvard physics students; purpose-built tutoring across two lessons, higher immediate tests with less time than in-class active learning.
claim_checks.evidence: Primary publisher indexed text identifies 194 eligible of 233 enrolled and the positive immediate comparison. Author identity is Greg Kestin, Kelly Miller, Anna Klales, Timothy Milbourne, Gregorio Ponti. The slide already limits the setting and endpoint.

slides.title: What do studies find overall?
slides.claim_category: published research claim with population and outcome limits

claim_checks.claim: 69 studies reviewed · 62 included in meta-analysis. Mostly university students; subjects, interventions and assessment methods varied considerably. Positive academic and motivation-related outcomes; high variation, publication bias and weak assessment designs limit lasting-understanding conclusions.
claim_checks.boundary: Publication-bias adjustments increased rather than decreased pooled effects. Slide correctly does not claim bias necessarily inflates the mean. Direct publisher fetch returned 403; primary-publisher indexed text was accessible.

claim_checks.evidence: Official publisher indexed text supports the verified portion. Direct publisher full text returned 403. Search returned a journal pre-proof mirror with 62, but that was not substituted for the cited version of record. This is an access limitation, not evidence of an error.

slides.title: Better answers can hide weaker learning
slides.claim_category: published research claim with population and outcome limits

claim_checks.claim: GPT Base improved practice scores by 48% relative to the control group. The same group scored 17% lower than the control. The safeguarded tutor largely removed this penalty, without a clear independent-test gain.
claim_checks.boundary: Relative percentages, not percentage-point changes. Closed-resource exams immediately followed each practice session. No delayed independent-learning conclusion.

claim_checks.claim: Bastani has a linked correction notice; selected numeric claims remain as shown in the published article.
GPT Base practice +48% and subsequent unassisted test −17%, relative to control; nearly 1,000 students, one Turkish school, four sessions.
claim_checks.evidence: Publisher abstract and experimental-design/main-results sections support the values and boundaries. The August 2025 correction concerns an author affiliation, not these results.

slides.title: Bibliography
slides.claim_category: bibliographic or resource metadata
checks: current official tool documentation and recorded-scope review

claim_checks.claim: Bastani has a linked correction notice; selected numeric claims remain as shown in the published article.
GPT Base practice +48% and subsequent unassisted test −17%, relative to control; nearly 1,000 students, one Turkish school, four sessions.
claim_checks.evidence: Publisher abstract and experimental-design/main-results sections support the values and boundaries. The August 2025 correction concerns an author affiliation, not these results.

claim_checks.claim: 194 eligible Harvard physics students; purpose-built tutoring across two lessons, higher immediate tests with less time than in-class active learning.
claim_checks.evidence: Primary publisher indexed text identifies 194 eligible of 233 enrolled and the positive immediate comparison. Author identity is Greg Kestin, Kelly Miller, Anna Klales, Timothy Milbourne, Gregorio Ponti. The slide already limits the setting and endpoint.

Official publisher indexed text supports the verified portion. Direct publisher full text returned 403. Search returned a journal pre-proof mirror with 62, but that was not substituted for the cited version of record. This is an access limitation, not evidence of an error.

claim_checks.claim: 2026 Huang paper exists; N=95, structured training, immediate AI-assisted electromagnetism revision rather than durable unassisted learning.
claim_checks.evidence: Publisher abstract identifies an RCT with 50 trained and 45 control students, followed by Doubao-assisted revision. Bibliographic title, ten authors, volume 13/article 62/DOI match.

claim_checks.claim: Retrieving passages during ordinary inference supplies context without itself updating model weights.
claim_checks.evidence: This is a correct operational distinction within the slides’ ordinary-inference/book-example scope. Lewis et al. also fine-tune RAG models, so it must not become a claim that every RAG architecture is never trained. The visible workshop repeatedly supplies the inference condition.

claim_checks.claim: Scientific Agent Skills is a 2026 preprint by Kassis, Agarwal, He, Patel and Brueckner.
claim_checks.evidence: Primary arXiv record shows those five authors, August 30 v1 and September 2 v2, the matching title and DOI. It explicitly reports no task-level effectiveness evaluation; the source registry correctly avoids claiming one.

claim_checks.claim: AI competency framework for students is a 2024 UNESCO publication by Fengchun Miao, Kelly Shiohira and Natalie Lao.
claim_checks.evidence: Official UNESCO record confirms identity, authors and year. This is a competency framework, not a learning-effectiveness experiment.

claim_checks.claim: Transformer Explainer by Cho et al. is a CHI 2026 conference paper with DOI 10.1145/3772318.3791725.
claim_checks.evidence: Author-hosted conference PDF and author-affiliation institutional publication record confirm the final title, venue, year and DOI. The official institutional record lists article 7/21 pages; the slide’s page shorthand does not change identity.

claim_checks.claim: Ouyang et al. (2022) is a NeurIPS 35 paper; DOI 10.52202/068431-2011 is valid despite its unfamiliar prefix.
claim_checks.evidence: The primary NeurIPS proceedings explicitly display that DOI with the matching title and author list.

corrections: C07: missing definition references added; 18-entry bibliography/audit aligned
